title: CAKUT Spectrum: PUJO, Posterior Urethral Valves and Vesicoureteral Reflux
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology

steps.say: Fetal pelvic dilatation provides early anatomical warning of developmental urinary obstruction.
steps.tx: Evaluate gestational pelvic measurements applying the standardized **Antenatal hydronephrosis grading (AP renal pelvic diameter)** protocols. Antenatal hydronephrosis on maternal ultrasound is graded by anteroposterior renal pelvic diameter (APRPD): >= 4-7 mm in second trimester and >= 7-10 mm in third trimester warrants postnatal surveillance to detect obstructive uropathy, renal dysplasia, or vesicoureteral reflux.

steps.say: Neonatal sonography requires deliberate scheduling to avoid transient physiological misinterpretation.
steps.tx: Structure early postnatal imaging following the strict **Postnatal ultrasound timing protocol** to ensure accuracy. Initial postnatal renal ultrasound is performed at 48-72 hours of life to avoid false-negative underestimation due to transient neonatal physiological oliguria, unless PUV is suspected where immediate emergent imaging and prompt catheter decompression are mandated on day one.

left.title: Standard Timing (48-72 Hours)
points: Accurate measurement of renal pelvis diameter

right.title: Urgent Day 1 Imaging
points: Indicated if posterior urethral valves suspected
Severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis on fetal scans

steps.say: Obstructive urethral membranes present exclusively in male neonates and distort the lower urinary tract.
steps.tx: Identify severe infravesical blockage recognizing the **Posterior urethral valves (PUV) keyhole sign** on ultrasound. PUV occurs exclusively in males, caused by congenital obstructing folds of the verumontanum (Type 1 Young classification), displaying a thick-walled trabeculated bladder and dilated posterior urethra (keyhole sign) on ultrasound, accompanied by bilateral hydroureteronephrosis and high risks of neonatal respiratory distress.

vis.alt: Hypospadias, cryptorchidism, posterior urethral valves and Wilms tumour features.
vis.caption: Posterior urethral valves sit in a wider CAKUT spectrum. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Relieving acute bladder outflow pressure prevents progressive renal parenchymal destruction.
steps.tx: Execute immediate bladder drainage following the **Urgent neonatal PUV decompression** guidelines at birth. Immediate neonatal management of PUV requires transurethral bladder catheterization (5-8 Fr feeding tube) followed by cystoscopic primary valve ablation; vesicostomy is performed if the urethra is too small, relieving elevated hydrostatic pressures to salvage developing renal parenchyma and restore electrolytes.

vis.title: Neonatal Posterior Urethral Valve Interventions
rows: Decompresses bladder if infant urethra is too small

steps.say: Dynamic diuretic renography differentiates functional stasis from true mechanical pelviureteric obstruction.
steps.tx: Quantify upper tract drainage dynamics using **Pelviureteric junction obstruction (PUJO) diuretic renography** protocols. PUJO is the most common cause of significant pediatric hydronephrosis; confirmed by 99mTc-MAG3 renography demonstrating prolonged washout half-time (T1/2 > 20 minutes) after furosemide (1 mg/kg), confirming true mechanical resistance across the pelviureteric junction rather than non-obstructive compliant pelvic flaccidity.

left.title: True PUJ Obstruction
points: Flat or rising curve after furosemide (1 mg/kg)

right.title: Non-Obstructive Dilatation
points: Compliant system managed safely with observation

steps.say: Surgical correction is indicated when serial functional evaluations demonstrate true parenchymal deterioration.
steps.tx: Establish definitive operative indications applying strict **Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty criteria** during surveillance. Surgical pyeloplasty is indicated for differential renal function < 40%, a fall of > 10% on serial scans, worsening hydronephrosis, or recurrent febrile urinary tract infections, resecting the aperistaltic obstructive adynamic pelviureteric segment and re-anastomosing the spatulated ureter to the renal pelvis.

nodes.label: Function < 40%, Loss > 10%, or Recurrent Febrile UTI

steps.say: Retrograde urinary flow staging guides medical surveillance and operative antireflux selection.
steps.tx: Grade retrograde ureteral incompetence applying the **International VUR classification grades (I-V)** under fluoroscopy. Micturating cystourethrogram (MCUG) grades vesicoureteral reflux from Grade I (reflux into non-dilated ureter) to Grade V (massive reflux, severe tortuosity, and complete loss of papillary impressions), defining the structural risk of intrarenal reflux and scarring during acute pyelonephritis episodes across pediatric cohorts.

vis.title: International Reflux Study VUR Classification
rows: Reflux into ureter only, no caliceal filling
Reflux into pelvis & calices without dilatation
Mild to moderate dilatation, blunting of fornices
Moderate risk, requires close infection vigilance
Moderate tortuosity, complete blunting of calices
High risk of progressive reflux nephropathy
Massive reflux, extreme tortuosity, effaced calices
Severe risk, surgical correction usually required

steps.say: Daily low-dose chemoprophylaxis cuts febrile urinary recurrences in half without altering established scars.
steps.tx: Prescribe targeted infection prevention based on **Continuous antibiotic prophylaxis (CAP) trials (RIVUR study)** findings. The RIVUR trial demonstrated that daily co-trimoxazole or nitrofurantoin prophylaxis in children with Grades II-IV VUR reduces recurrent febrile UTIs by 50% without altering renal scarring, providing critical protection against recurrent urosepsis while awaiting spontaneous maturation of the vesicoureteral junction.

vis.title: RIVUR Trial Prophylaxis Evidence
rows: Children with Grade II to IV VUR
Emphasizes prompt treatment of acute infections
